# eba-cli

eba-cli is a command-line tool for Expo and React Native developers who want to use Xcode Cloud as a free alternative to EAS Build when they hit the monthly build limit.

## Why it exists

Expo EAS Build free tier is limited to 15 builds/month. Apple gives every Apple Developer account member 25 free compute hours/month on Xcode Cloud (~75–100 iOS builds/month). eba-cli provides a CLI interface to manage and trigger Xcode Cloud builds without needing Xcode IDE or the App Store Connect web UI. It works on any OS — Windows, macOS, Linux.

## What it is NOT

- Not an Expo or Apple official tool
- Not a replacement for Xcode or the full EAS suite
- Not a tool for Android builds (iOS / Xcode Cloud only)

## How it works

eba-cli authenticates with Apple ID using the same SRP protocol as EAS CLI (via @expo/apple-utils). After login, it communicates with the App Store Connect internal API (iris) and the public REST API to manage CI products, workflows, and build runs. Session is cached locally for 1 hour.

Build configuration (ascAppId) is read from the project's existing eas.json file — no new config file is required.

## Commands

### eba build
Triggers an Xcode Cloud build from the terminal.
- Reads ascAppId from eas.json (submit.[env].ios.ascAppId or build.[env].ios.ascAppId)
- Warns if ios/ has uncommitted changes (Xcode Cloud pulls from last pushed commit)
- Prompts user to select a workflow if multiple exist
- Prints a direct link to track the build in App Store Connect

### eba prebuild
Generates ios/ci_scripts/ — shell scripts required by Xcode Cloud to set up the build environment for a React Native / Expo project.
- ci_post_clone.sh: detects Node.js (nvm/Homebrew), runs npm install, installs CocoaPods, patches fmt headers for Apple Clang 15+
- ci_pre_xcodebuild.sh: syncs Manifest.lock, sets build number via agvtool
- ci_post_build.sh: logs build metadata
- App name is read from app.json and substituted into the scripts
- Run this once after expo prebuild generates the ios/ folder, then push ios/ to GitHub

### eba workflow
Creates an Xcode Cloud workflow via the App Store Connect API.
- No browser or Xcode IDE required
- Prompts for workflow name, scheme, branch trigger, and TestFlight distribution option

### eba devices
Lists registered iOS/iPadOS devices in the Apple Developer account.
- --register: register a new device via UDID (QR code flow or manual entry)

### eba certs
Lists iOS distribution and development certificates.
- --revoke: select and revoke a certificate

### eba profiles
Lists iOS provisioning profiles.
- --delete: select and delete a profile

### eba bundle-ids
Lists registered bundle IDs (App IDs).
- --register: register a new bundle ID
- --filter <query>: filter by bundle ID or name
- --capabilities: show capabilities per bundle ID

## Configuration

No dedicated config file. Uses the project's existing eas.json:

```json
{
  "submit": {
    "production": {
      "ios": {
        "ascAppId": "1234567890"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

ascAppId is the numeric App Store Connect app ID found in the URL:
https://appstoreconnect.apple.com/apps/1234567890/...

## Auth

- Apple ID login via @expo/apple-utils (SRP protocol, same as EAS CLI)
- Session cached for 1 hour in ~/.eba-cli/config.json
- No API key required for eba build, eba prebuild, eba devices, eba certs, eba profiles, eba bundle-ids

## Requirements

- Node.js >= 18
- Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year)
- App registered on App Store Connect
- Xcode Cloud enabled for the app (App Store Connect → app → Xcode Cloud → Get Started)
- Source code on GitHub, Bitbucket, or GitLab (required by Xcode Cloud)

## Typical workflow

1. Run expo prebuild to generate ios/ folder (standard Expo step)
2. Run eba prebuild to add ios/ci_scripts/
3. Push ios/ to GitHub
4. Run eba workflow once to create a workflow on Xcode Cloud
5. Run eba build whenever a new build is needed
